newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks hit third record in row.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks hit third record in row.

text.p: Swiss shares posted their third record session in a row and for the first time ended above the important 4,900 point level in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI).

The market took a positive view of a patch of U.S. economic data and this led to a further improvement in interest rate prospects. A firmer start on Wall Street and positive corporate results were another factor for the rise.
"We may well be heading toward 5,000 points given the good fundamentals," a trader noted.
The SMI ended up 55.9 points, or 1.14 percent, to 4,953.5 and the broad SPI rose 32.82 points, or 1.06 percent, to end at 3,127.47.
The SMI finished slightly below its intra-day high of 4,958.2. Total bourse turnover reached 2,33 billion francs.
UBS bearer shares led the active list, continuing their recent bull run. The stock ended up 12 francs to 1,407 on speculative buing and recommendations.
CS Group recovered from initial switches into UBS, ending up 1.25 francs to 167.25. SBC also firmed.
Swiss Re, which reported a 33 percent rise in group net profit to 1.459 billion francs after the bourse closed, ended 40 francs, or 2.34 percent, higher at 1,746 francs.
A trader said the result was above market expectations.
Insurer Zurich turned initial losses due to profit taking into a closing gain of one franc to 485 francs.

Among pharmaceuticals and chemicals, Ciba SC stood out, posting a jump of 4.25 francs, or 3.35 percent, to 131.25 francs. Novartis registered shares also saw a strong rise of 36 francs to 1,978. Roche cerfificates added 60 francs to 12,510.
Nestle ended 16 francs higher at 1,806, but SMH bearer shares ended off three francs at 832.
